Former Apple design chief Jony Ive has long described his vision for the iPhone as "a single sheet of glass." Even though Ive has left the company, it is widely believed that Apple still holds onto this goal, and the Liquid Glass design is Apple's software preparation ahead of new hardware.

We have already seen numerous reports suggesting that the 20th anniversary edition iPhone may, in various ways, come significantly closer to Apple's vision, and the latest piece of news may add another piece to this puzzle……

What we expect

Initially there were speculations that Apple might launch the 20th anniversary edition iPhone as a standalone model, but more recent reports suggest that all the features designed to achieve a glass slab appearance will be incorporated into the iPhone 19 Pro. To make things even more complicated, some believe that to mark this milestone, Apple will skip the iPhone 19 naming entirely and go straight to iPhone 20 Pro.

Given how far away we are from the launch, these reports are still speculative in nature, but the most important design feature is expected to be a screen that curves on all four sides, making the bezels completely disappear to create the illusion of a borderless design.

It seems almost certain that Apple will finally be able to embed the Face ID module under the screen this year, and there are also expectations that the front camera and speaker can be hidden beneath the display as well.

All of these combined would create a very convincing "single sheet of glass" appearance.

Glass back

Leaker Fixed Focus Digital now says there's another component: a return to a glass back instead of the aluminum alloy used in recent models.

Although a glass back would make the phone more prone to shattering if dropped, it undoubtedly helps realise the "single sheet of glass" design philosophy. In pursuit of a futuristic-looking design, would you consider this trade-off acceptable? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
